title: Challenge: run a multi-container app with Compose
intro: A compose.yaml in this folder defines a 'web' and a 'db' service. Bring the whole stack up, inspect it, read logs, step inside, and tear it down, one file, one command. (Commands are checked, not executed. Both 'docker compose' and 'docker-compose' are accepted.)

steps.instruction: Start the whole stack in the background (detached).
steps.success:
[+] Running 3/3
 Network app_default   Created
 Container app-db-1     Started
 Container app-web-1    Started
steps.fail: docker compose up -d brings everything up detached.

steps.instruction: List the stack's containers and their state.
steps.success:
NAME         SERVICE   STATUS         PORTS
app-db-1     db        running        5432/tcp
app-web-1    web       running        0.0.0.0:8080->80/tcp
steps.fail: docker compose ps shows the stack's containers.

steps.instruction: Read the logs of just the 'web' service.
steps.success:
app-web-1  | listening on :80
app-web-1  | connected to db:5432

steps.instruction: Open a shell inside the running 'web' service.
steps.success:
/ #
you're inside app-web-1; the host 'db' resolves to the other service automatically

steps.instruction: Tear the whole stack down (containers + network).
steps.success:
[+] Running 3/3
 Container app-web-1   Removed
 Container app-db-1    Removed
 Network app_default   Removed
steps.fail: docker compose down removes everything the stack created.

done: Solved! up -> ps -> logs -> exec -> down. Compose turns a multi-container app into one declarative file: services share a network and reach each other by service name (web talks to 'db' directly).
